newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Royal Dutch lower on earnings.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Royal Dutch lower on earnings.

text.p: Royal Dutch Petroleum Co was trading lower for a second day, its American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) still suffering from the repercussions of its disappointing quarterly earnings, traders said Friday.
The oil company's American Depositary Receipt was trading 1-3/16 lower at 53-7/8 in midday trading.
Meanwhile, the Shell Group was down 1-3/16 at 42.
On Thursday, Royal Dutch/Shell Group reported current cost income excluding special items of 1.140 billion sterling, much to the disappointment of investors.
The dealer said he suspected Royal Dutch was also hurt by program trading since it was listed on a major market index.
European drug companies were also lower.

Swedish drug company Astra AB was down 1-3/16 at 17-7/8. On Friday, it reported a 13-percent rise in sales to 21.47 billion crowns, in line with expectations, but its four-percent increase in pre-tax profits to 7.01 billion crowns was lower than forecasts of 7.18 billion.
Glaxo Wellcome Plc was 1-5/16 lower at 40-5/8, while Zeneca Group Plc was down 2-13/16 at 95-1/8.
Latin American ADRs were much calmer in comparison.
"They are reasonably firm," said another trader.
Telebras SA was down 3-1/4 at 137 amid what the trader said were "small currency jitters," and Telefonos de Mexico was down 1-10/16 at 53-9/16.
Decliners led advancers 377 to 136n amond 814 ADRs.
The ADR group was down 0.87 percent amid a volume of 43.3 million ADRs. ADRs enable U.S. trade in foreign stock.
